claims.text: A tungsten-free refractory HEA containing Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Al can serve as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The initial material is a conventional tungsten-containing refractory HEA designed for high-temperature performance.
The initial tungsten-containing refractory HEA is designed for irradiation resistance.
Tungsten and certain other alloying elements generate long-lived radioactive isotopes under neutron irradiation.
Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Al are lower-activation refractory substitutes for tungsten.
Fusion-reactor plasma-facing components operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K.
Fusion-reactor plasma-facing components are exposed to neutron irradiation.
Refractory HEAs can possess strong mechanical properties and thermal stability in hostile high-temperature environments.
High configurational entropy contributes to solid-solution formation in HEAs.
A stabilized microstructure and high configurational entropy govern both refractory strength and radiation resistance in the proposed tungsten-free alloy.
The alloy's stabilized microstructure and high configurational entropy limit the formation of long-lived radionuclides.
Removing tungsten reduces the formation of long-lived radioactive isotopes under neutron bombardment.
A high-entropy design will retain high-temperature mechanical properties after tungsten is replaced by Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Al.
A high-entropy design will retain irradiation tolerance after tungsten is replaced by Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Al.
The tungsten-free HEA will have high-temperature strength and ductility comparable to tungsten-containing alloys.
The tungsten-free HEA will produce significantly fewer long-lived radioactive isotopes than tungsten-containing alloys during neutron irradiation.
Tungsten is a leading plasma-facing material because of its high melting temperature, low erosion rate, and low tritium retention.
Tungsten plasma-facing materials suffer from brittle behavior and low fracture toughness.
Standard tungsten-based plasma-facing materials suffer from problematic long-lived activation.
The degree of activation reduction and the mechanical performance under reactor conditions remain uncertain and require experimental verification.
